subject.title: Add a retraction window for forwarded exec approvals (agent-cancellable hold before prompt delivery)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in forwarded exec approval hold/retract window, and where should agent retraction authority live?
rationale: The request is not a broken existing contract; it adds config and approval-boundary semantics that affect Gateway protocol, forwarding reliability, auditability, and Codex/native approval behavior.

options.title: Design opt-in core hold/retract
options.body: Add `holdMs` defaulting to 0 plus a narrowly authorized retraction path, with explicit audit logs and tests for fail-open delivery and fail-closed execution.

options.title: Keep immediate delivery
options.body: Reject the new surface and preserve the simpler invariant that approval prompts are sent as soon as they are registered.

options.title: Defer to preflight/auto-review only
options.body: Avoid a new retraction RPC and instead reduce junk prompts through existing auto-review, allowlist, or command-shaping behavior.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core hold/retract
recommendation.body: Add `holdMs` defaulting to 0 plus a narrowly authorized retraction path, with explicit audit logs and tests for fail-open delivery and fail-closed execution.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans shared Gateway approval helpers and Codex app-server approval semantics where steipete has direct recent history.
